questionsToConsider: Which parts of your service do customers mention most, and should they replace the rows in the rating grid?
Should the question about staying a year from now match your renewal cycle, such as the next contract or the next season?
Who contacts a customer who says something nearly made them leave, and how soon?
Do you want to send this to every customer or only to those past their first renewal?
guide.howToUseResponses: Pull out every response where something came close to making the customer leave, or where they are unsure about the next year, and treat it as an at-risk account: read what triggered it and what they want fixed first, and get the owner of that account to reply. Across everyone else, compare the reasons people stay with how often they use you. Customers who stay only because switching is a hassle are less secure than they look.
customizeSteps: Edit the reasons for staying so they describe what you actually sell, and keep the switching-hassle option since it is an honest warning sign.
Add the customer's account name or plan as a hidden field so each at-risk answer can be traced back.
Send it a month or two before renewals come round, then export the at-risk answers to CSV for your account team.

faqs.q: What questions should a customer retention survey include?
faqs.a: How much value customers get, why they stay, how you perform on the things that matter to them, and whether anything has nearly made them leave. That last one is the question most surveys avoid and the one that tells you the most.

faqs.q: When should I run a customer retention survey?
faqs.a: Once or twice a year, and ideally before a renewal date rather than after it, so there is still time to act on what people say.

faqs.q: What is the difference between retention and satisfaction surveys?
faqs.a: A satisfaction survey asks how happy people are. A retention survey asks whether they will stay and what could change that, which is a more useful question for planning.

faqs.q: How do I find at-risk customers from the results?
faqs.a: Filter for anyone who said something nearly made them leave or who is unsure they will be a customer next year, and look at low value scores alongside falling usage. Those accounts deserve a personal follow-up.
